title: Replay the complete P104 proposal 4.75x faster with explicit engines
body:
The entire PR6453 proposal now replays through explicit native, forward-row and pricing dependencies. It regenerates every word and receipt and preserves the complete scientific output and progress transcript. Median full-command runtime falls from **166.78 s to 35.09 s (4.75×)** in three alternating fresh-process pairs. All six output hashes agree; ranges are 154.06–241.90 s and 29.43–39.73 s.

This closes the full-path integration gap left by component-only tests. It retains every source constructor/regression and corruption control, owned lifetimes and zero scratch, 799 transpose columns, 2,941 native maps, 208 main adapters, 7,488 physical contacts, the caller and independent module, both price engines, compiler and all 54 strict/four functional outer predicates. Native and physical receipts are regenerated, not loaded as old acceptance answers.

The untouched full source is the baseline. Four declared interface edits are checked byte for byte; no imported module or class is patched. Component methods and gains remain credited to PR6479, PR6501, PR6505 and PR6507. No new arithmetic method or kappa is claimed.

Local verification includes an actual untouched-baseline comparison, registered CPython 3.12 normal/optimized complete replay, exact committed bytes and modes, official export/input coverage, read-only Git-free empty-PATH normal/optimized replay and exported-source corruption rejection. The benchmark includes startup, imports, authentication, archive extraction, full execution and serialization. No timing threshold runs in CI.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-complete-fast-replay`. Add `--compare-baseline` to the direct `verify.py` command to repeat the slower untouched-source comparison. All samples and executed source bindings are retained.

Limits: source-specific engineering and finite replay, not independent scientific acceptance or a physical multiplier. All five framework assumptions remain. Selected PR6030 is unchanged. No Lean, Docker or optional full-history preflight is claimed in this shallow checkout. No known fragile workaround is used.

PR6453 is by Erwan L. with Claude assistance and builds on Rohan Arun's PR6417. Credit David Arias, Cinna Davis, Gareth Davidson, Charles Bethin, Wentao Li, zxv, Cao Yifan, Jacob Alan Sussman and the retained lineage. Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Exact notices and source proofs remain in inputs.

Canonical main 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, revision 8 and live overlap through PR6522 were rechecked before publication. [Claim and updates](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5600#discussioncomment-19364125). Next: profile the remaining complete-path cost before choosing another mechanism.
